questions.prompt: Which task is an example of unsupervised learning?
choices: Predicting house prices from square footage and number of bedrooms
Grouping customers into segments based on purchasing behavior
Classifying emails as spam or not spam
Predicting whether a loan applicant will default using historical repayment data
questions.correct_answer: Grouping customers into segments based on purchasing behavior
questions.explanation: Unsupervised learning finds hidden patterns or intrinsic structures in input data without labeled outcomes; clustering customers is a classic example.

distractor_rationales.Predicting house prices from square foot: This is regression — a supervised learning task because it uses labeled output (prices) to train the model.
distractor_rationales.Classifying emails as spam or not spam: This is classification — a supervised learning task requiring labeled examples of spam and non-spam emails.
distractor_rationales.Predicting whether a loan applicant will: This is binary classification with labeled outcomes (defaulted/did not default), making it supervised learning.

questions.prompt: What is the primary purpose of a validation set?
choices: To provide final, unbiased evaluation of model performance after training and selection
To tune hyperparameters and select the best model among candidates
To compute gradients during backpropagation
To initialize model weights before training begins
questions.correct_answer: To tune hyperparameters and select the best model among candidates
questions.explanation: The validation set is used during model development to assess performance across different hyperparameter configurations and guide model selection without touching the test set.

distractor_rationales.To provide final, unbiased evaluation of: That is the role of the test set, not the validation set.
distractor_rationales.To compute gradients during backpropagat: Gradients are computed using the training set, not the validation set.
distractor_rationales.To initialize model weights before train: Weights are typically initialized randomly or via schemes like Xavier/Glorot — unrelated to the validation set.

A linear model fails to capture a clear quadratic trend in the data and performs poorly on both training and test sets
A model performs equally well (≈80%) on both training and test data
A decision tree is pruned aggressively and generalizes poorly to new examples
questions.correct_answer: A model achieves 99% accuracy on training data but only 55% on unseen test data
questions.explanation: Overfitting occurs when a model learns noise or idiosyncrasies in the training data, resulting in high training performance but poor generalization to new data.

distractor_rationales.A linear model fails to capture a clear: This describes underfitting — the model is too simple to capture the underlying pattern.
distractor_rationales.A model performs equally well (≈80%) on: This suggests good generalization, not overfitting.
distractor_rationales.A decision tree is pruned aggressively a: Aggressive pruning usually reduces overfitting; poor generalization here likely reflects underfitting, not overfitting.

questions.prompt: Which loss function is most commonly used for binary classification tasks in logistic regression?
choices: Mean Squared Error (MSE)
Hinge Loss
Cross-Entropy Loss
Kullback-Leibler Divergence
questions.explanation: Cross-entropy loss (also called log loss) directly measures the dissimilarity between predicted class probabilities and true binary labels, making it ideal for logistic regression.

distractor_rationales.Mean Squared Error (MSE): MSE can be used but is less appropriate for classification because it penalizes confident wrong predictions less severely and lacks probabilistic interpretation.
distractor_rationales.Hinge Loss: Hinge loss is used in support vector machines (SVMs), not standard logistic regression.
distractor_rationales.Kullback-Leibler Divergence: KL divergence is related but not identical; cross-entropy is the standard choice, and KL divergence assumes both distributions are known and normalized.

questions.prompt: Why might you apply logarithmic transformation to a highly right-skewed feature (e.g., income)?
choices: To convert categorical values into numeric codes
To reduce the influence of outliers and make the distribution more symmetric
To increase the dimensionality by adding polynomial terms
To ensure all feature values are integers
questions.correct_answer: To reduce the influence of outliers and make the distribution more symmetric
questions.explanation: Log transformation compresses large values and expands small ones, mitigating skewness and improving model assumptions (e.g., linearity, homoscedasticity) in many algorithms.

distractor_rationales.To convert categorical values into numer: That is handled by encoding techniques (e.g., one-hot or label encoding), not log transforms.
distractor_rationales.To increase the dimensionality by adding: Polynomial features add new columns; log transformation modifies an existing feature without increasing dimensionality.
distractor_rationales.To ensure all feature values are integer: Logarithms of positive numbers are typically non-integer real numbers; this is not a goal of log transformation.

questions.prompt: In a medical screening test for a rare disease, why might accuracy be misleading?
choices: Because it ignores class imbalance and may be inflated by correctly predicting the majority (healthy) class
Because it cannot be computed when the model outputs probabilities
Because it requires a confusion matrix with exactly four entries
Because it is undefined for multi-class problems
questions.correct_answer: Because it ignores class imbalance and may be inflated by correctly predicting the majority (healthy) class
questions.explanation: With rare diseases, even a naive model predicting 'no disease' for everyone may achieve >99% accuracy — masking failure to detect actual cases.

distractor_rationales.Because it cannot be computed when the m: Accuracy is computed from hard predictions (e.g., thresholded probabilities), not raw probabilities — it’s fully computable.
distractor_rationales.Because it requires a confusion matrix w: While binary accuracy uses a 2×2 confusion matrix, accuracy itself is just a scalar derived from it — no structural requirement beyond correct/incorrect counts.
distractor_rationales.Because it is undefined for multi-class: Accuracy is well-defined and widely used for multi-class classification (proportion of correct predictions).

questions.prompt: Which statement best describes high bias in a machine learning model?
choices: The model is overly sensitive to small fluctuations in the training data
The model consistently makes incorrect predictions due to oversimplification
The model achieves near-perfect accuracy on training data but fails on test data
The model's predictions vary widely across different training sets
questions.correct_answer: The model consistently makes incorrect predictions due to oversimplification
questions.explanation: High bias reflects systematic error from assumptions that are too strong or simplistic (e.g., fitting a line to quadratic data), leading to underfitting.

distractor_rationales.The model is overly sensitive to small f: That describes high variance, not high bias.
distractor_rationales.The model achieves near-perfect accuracy: That is characteristic of high variance (overfitting).
distractor_rationales.The model's predictions vary widely acro: This is also a hallmark of high variance.

questions.prompt: What role does the learning rate play in gradient descent?
choices: It determines how many iterations the algorithm runs before stopping
It scales the size of parameter updates in the direction opposite to the gradient
It controls whether the algorithm uses batch, mini-batch, or stochastic updates
It defines the mathematical form of the loss function
questions.correct_answer: It scales the size of parameter updates in the direction opposite to the gradient
questions.explanation: The learning rate multiplies the gradient to determine the step size taken toward minimizing loss — too large causes overshooting; too small slows convergence.

distractor_rationales.It determines how many iterations the al: Iteration count is set by the stopping criterion (e.g., max epochs or loss threshold), not the learning rate.
distractor_rationales.It controls whether the algorithm uses b: That is determined by the data sampling strategy, not the learning rate.
distractor_rationales.It defines the mathematical form of the: The loss function is chosen separately (e.g., MSE, cross-entropy); the learning rate operates *on* the gradient of that function.

questions.prompt: What does 'information gain' measure when splitting a node in a decision tree?
choices: The reduction in Gini impurity after the split
The increase in prediction variance introduced by the split
The reduction in entropy (or uncertainty) about the target variable after the split
The absolute difference between mean target values in left and right child nodes
questions.correct_answer: The reduction in entropy (or uncertainty) about the target variable after the split
questions.explanation: Information gain quantifies how much uncertainty (measured by entropy) in the target label is reduced by a given split — higher gain means a more informative split.

distractor_rationales.The reduction in Gini impurity after the: That is Gini gain — a different, though related, splitting criterion; information gain specifically uses entropy.
distractor_rationales.The increase in prediction variance intr: Variance is not used in standard decision tree splitting for classification; this mischaracterizes the objective.
distractor_rationales.The absolute difference between mean tar: That relates to regression splits or simple heuristics, not information gain in classification trees.

questions.prompt: How does L2 regularization (Ridge) affect model weights?
choices: It forces many weights to become exactly zero, performing feature selection
It shrinks all weights toward zero but rarely sets them to zero
It prevents the model from using any features by setting all weights to zero
It increases the magnitude of large weights while reducing small ones
questions.correct_answer: It shrinks all weights toward zero but rarely sets them to zero
questions.explanation: L2 regularization adds a penalty proportional to the squared magnitude of weights, encouraging small but non-zero coefficients — it discourages large weights without inducing sparsity.

distractor_rationales.It forces many weights to become exactly: That is the behavior of L1 (Lasso) regularization, not L2.
distractor_rationales.It prevents the model from using any fea: That would produce a trivial model; L2 penalizes large weights but permits non-zero solutions.
distractor_rationales.It increases the magnitude of large weig: L2 uniformly penalizes weight magnitude — larger weights incur disproportionately higher penalties, so they are shrunk more (not increased).
